case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 27.10.2009 passed by the High Court Division in civil Revision No-3777 of 2001.)
full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J. This civil Appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated 27.10.2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No-3777 of 2001 making the Rue absolute and thereby setting aside the judgment and decree dated 16.04.2001 passed by the learned Districted Judge, Pabna, in other Class Appeal No-90 of 1999 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Chatmohor, Pabna in other Class Suit No-89 of 1997 dismissing.

2. Facts giving rise to this civil in short are that:

<u>3. The present appellants on 19.07.1977 instituted other class Suit No-394 of 1977 for simple deliration of their title in the suit land, stating inter alia that the suit land described in schedule 'Ka' to the plaint appertaining to D.S. Khatyian No-830 belonged to Jhabu Pramanik alias Jhabu Sheikh who died leaving behind two named Erfan Bibi. But the D.S Khatian was wrongly prepared in the name of Tasiruddin alone. However, Tasiruddin and Alimuddin borrowed some money from Narendra Nath Das, Karta of the joint family; that when loan Narendra Nath Das filed Suit No-619 of 1920 in the 2nd Court of Munsif, Pabna Sadar and obtained a decree; that before realization of the detail amount Alimuddin died leaving behind his widow, Sobjan, a daughter Tuni Bibi and brother Tasiruddin thus, Narendra Nath Das filed execution Case No-139 of 1921 against them wherein the 'Ka' schedule property was put into auction, that at the time of auction sale Aziron and Asiron, the two daughters of Erfan Bibi (sister of Tasiruddin and Alimuddin) raised their claim against the sale of the entire land and accordingly, their share were excluded from the said auction was purchased by Narendra Nath on 10.03.1922 and pursuant to his application dated 11.03.1922, possession of the same was delivered to him by the Court; that thereafter the said Narendra Nath died leaving behind his son, Surendra Nath and two brothers Lalit Mohon and Ganendr Nath and all of them settled 0.51 acre of larid be way of pattan to Moniruddin and Nasiruddin which was recorded in SA Khatian No-1548, that apart from the said pattan Lalit Mohon transferred 0.18 acre of land from plot No-1993 and 0.11 acre from plot No-2015, altogether 0.29 acre of land by registered deed of sale to Monirudddin and thus, the total land pur-chased by Moniruddin was recorded in his name in S.A Khatian No-1549 but at the time of survey, 1.40 acres of land in S.A. Khatian No-1550 was wrongly recorded in the name of defendants for which the defendants denied the title of the plaintiffs in the 'Kha' schedule land in the month of Jaistha, 1384 B,S. and hence the plaintiffs instituted other Class Suit No-394 of 1977 on 19.07.1977 in the 3rd court of Munsif, Pabna. The plaintiffs, amended the plaint and enhanced the calculation of the suit from plaint and enhanced the valuation of the suit from Tk. 2000/- to Tk. 21000/- by order No-42 dated 6.7.1983. Thereafter the suit was transferred to the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Bera and was renumbered as other Class Suit No-23 of 1991. However, during the pendency of the suit the plaintiffs were dispossessed from the suit land on 10.10.1977 and, as such, the plaint again filed application for amendment of the plaint on 25.02.1992 for incorporating the prayer for recovery of khas possession which was allowed by the Court on 08.03.1992 for incorporating the prayer for recovery of khas possession which was allowed by the Court on 25.02.1992 with direction to deposit court fee of Tk. 2039/- by the next date and the same was deposited on 8.03.1992. Ultimately the suit was transferred to the Court of Assistant Judge, Chatmpohor, Pabna, and re-numbered as other Class Suit No-89 of 1997.</u>

4. The defendant No-7 appeared in the suit on 08.03.1992 and contested the suit by filling written statement denying the material allegations made in the plant contested the suit is not maintainable in its present form and it is barred by limitation. It is claimed that the suit land belonged to Tasiruddin Pramanik alias Tasiruddin Sheikh (Father of defendant No-7) as his self acquired property which was recorded in his name in C.S. Khatian No-830 and the suit property was neither put into auction nor it was identical to or attracts the schedule of the alleged certificate case.

5. The trial Court on consideration of the evidence on record, dismissed the suit by judgment and decree dated 11.10.1999. against the same the plaintiffs preferred other Class Appeal No-90 of 1999 before the learned District Judge, Pabna which was ultimately heard and allowed by the learned Joint District Judge, Pabna reversing the judgment and decree of the trail Court and decreeing the suit on contest against defendant No-7 and exported against the rest with direction upon the defendant respondents to be evicted, by judgment and decree dated 16.04.2001. 6. The plaintiffs decree holders, there-after, filed Title Execution Case No-1 of 2001. During the pendency of the said execution case, the plaintiff decree holder No-1, Surendra Nath, died and as such his two sons namely (1) Sree Sukumar Das and (ii) Sree Sukanto Kumar Das were substituted in his place in the execution case. The executing court ultimately allowed the execution case and handed over possession of the suit land in favour of the decree holders vide order dated 26.06.2001.

7. On the other hand against the judgment and decree dated 16.04.2001 passed in other Class Appeal No-90 of 1999 by the learned Joint District Judge, Pabna, the defendant No-7, on 12.07.2001, after the execution case was over, filed Civil Revision No-3777 of 2001 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule and stay, which, ultimately has been made absolute upon setting aside the judgment and decree of the Court of appeal below and affirming those of the trial Court by the impugned judgment and order dated 27.10.2009.

8. Hence, the plaintiffs as appellant filed Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No-2315 of 2009 and obtained leave giving rise to the instant Civil Appeal.

<u>9. Mr. Mahbuby Alam, the learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-appellants submits that when the appellate Court upon assessing the evidence both oral and documentary on record and also upon considering the pro-visions of law reversed the finding of the trial Court on the question of limitation holding that the suit was not barred by limitation, for late payment of the advaloum Court fees, the finding of the High Court Division that the court of Appeal below due to non application of judicial mind came to a wrong and erroneous finding which is liable to be interfered by the court is completely due to non appreciation and non consideration of the evidence on record and law and as such the same is erroneous. Mr. Alam next submits that the High Court Division further erred in law in not considering the fact that pursuant to the decree of appellate court, admittedly the plaintiff appellants, initiated Title Execution case No-1 of 2001 as per law and the plaintiff decree holder No-1, Surendra Nath Das having died. on 21.04.2001 during the pendency of the said execution case his two sons (1) Sree Sukumar Das and (ii) Sree Sukanto Kumar Das having been sub situated as his surviving legal heirs and the executing court having allowed the execution case and thereby handed over the possession of the suit land in favour of the plaintiff decree holders vide order dated 21.06.2001 within the full knowledge of the contesting defendant No-7 the decision of the High Court Division is not sustainable in law hence the same is liable to be set aside. He lastly submits that the High Court Division is not sustainable in law hence the same is liable to be set aside. He lasly submits that the High Court Division without considering the fact that all the amendment application were allowed in presence of the defendants who filled hazira and received the copy of the same with objection but did not oppose the prayer at the hearing and as such the suit was taken out of the list of peremptory hearing and was field for filling additional written statement, if any, and the defendant having not filed any additional written statement to that extent made the Rule absolute which is error apparent on the face of the record and is liable to be set aside.</u>

10. 25.02.92, after the period of limitation is barred by limitation. The appellate court, on the other hand, without proper assessment of the material on record reversed the findings of the trial court on importing completely a new case based on false, fabricated and absurd story which is beyond the scope of law. He submits that plaintiffs admitted in his evidence that initially the suit was only for declaration of title valued at Tk. 2000/- and the same was subsequently enhanced to Tk. 21,0000/-by amendment and subsequently the suit being transferred to Bera Adalat was renumbered as Suit No-60 of 1983 where it was decreed ex parte and the said decree was set aside in miscellaneous case under order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure which was subsequently dis-missed and then on appeal the same was resorted. He submits that the plaintiff initially instituted the suit land and subsequently the plaint was amended vide courts order No-13 dated 25.02.1992 thereby framing the suit for declaration of title and recovery of khash possession alleging dispossession on 10.10.1977. This amended was brought admittedly after more than 14 years which is beyond the period of limitation as prescribed by law. Moreover pursuant to order No-13 dated 25.02.1992 the Court fee was paid on 08.03.1992 and 14.03.1992 which was beyond the time fixed by the Court. He further submits that as the plaintiff, as P.W 1, admitted in his cross examination that আদালতে নরেন্দ্র নাথ যে দখল পায় তার দখলনামা জমা দেয় নাই।he thus failed to prove as to when their predecessor Narendra Nath over possession of the suit land. Thus where there is no document of taking over possession by vendor any transfer utterly dialed to prove their case. Thus he submits that the plaintiffs, by practicing fraud upon the court incorporated a new story of dispossession and accordingly managed to obtain a judgment from the Court of appeal below which has no legal basis thus the High Court division did not commit any error in not considering the alleged repossession and thereby rightly passed the impugned judgment which is not liable to be set aside.

11. On examination of the materials on record, it appears that the plaintiffs instituted the suit on 19.07.1977, initially for declaration of title fixing the value at Tk. 2000/- thereafter by amendments the value was enhanced to Tk. 21000/- on 06.071983 in the original Court and then after the first transfer the prayer for recovery of khas possession was added vide order No-13 dated 25.02.1992 as they were dispossessed on 10.10.1977 and the Court directed the plaintiffs to deposit deficit fee of Tk-2039/- by the next date fixed which the plaintiffs complied with.

12. The trial Court in determining the suit framed as many as six issues and took evidence of the parties. The issues were (i) whether the suit is maintainable in its present forms (ii) whether the suit is bad for defect of parties (iii) whiter the suit is barred by limitation (iv) whether the plaintiffs have title in the suit land (v) whether the plaintiffs were dispossessed on the date as claimed and before dispossessed on the date as claimed and before dispossession whether the plaintiffs were in possession and (vi) whether the plaintiffs were in possession and (vi) whether the plaintiffs are on titled to the relief for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession.

13. In the suit the plaintiffs adduced 4 PWs and the defendants adduced 3 Des in support of their respective claims and country claims. On consideration of materials on record although the trial Court found the plaintiffs possession in the suit land before the date of dispossession and also found that the suit is maintainable in its present form since the plaintiffs paid advolarem court fees after being dispossessed but dispossession being 10.10.1977 and the amendment to that aspect has been made in the plaint by order No-13 dated 25.02.1992, which is after a lapse of 14 years four months and 15 days, beyond the period of limitation of 12 years as spelt out in law. Thus the suit is barred by limitation.

14. The appellate court on consideration of materials on record allowed the appeal having concurrently found the plaintiffs title and possession in the suit land where-from they have been disposed and this set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court holding that the amendment was done in accordance with law and since payment of deficit advolurem court fees have been paid in march 1993, after the amendment was allowed on 25.02.1992, with permission of the court, the suit can-not be dismissed for being barred by limitation. Whenever court fee is found to be inadequate the suit may not be proceeded with but the suit shall not be time barred for that particular reason only.

15. From the material on record it appears that though the Courts below observed that the amendment in respect of dispossession was allowed on 06.07.1983 but actually from the record it appears that such amendment was prayed for and allowed on 25.02.1992. the amendment sought for and allowed on 06.07.1983 was actually regarding enhancement of the valuation of the suit, not in respect of dispossession and adding the prayer for recovery of khas possession. Record also shows that the suit was instituted on 19.07.1977 for declaration of title only ad the plaintiffs claimed that during the pendency of the said suit they were dispossessed from the suit land on 10.10.1977. Although after such dispossession the plaintiffs amended the plaint but that was for enhancing the valuation of the plaint which was allowed on 06.07.1983. The amendment for adding the prayer for recovery of khas possession was actually filed and allowed on contest vide Order No-13 dated 25.02.1992 after the suit was transferred to the Court of Assistant Judge, Bera, Pabna and renumbered as other suit No-23 of 1991 wherein the plaintiffs were also directed to put in the deficit court fees by the next date.

<u>16. Generally all material facts and particular are to be stated in the pleading. But because of mistake or inadvertence or sub-sequent development or to meet the case made out by the opponent, requirement for amendment of pleading may arise. Generally a prayer for amendment is considered liberally for bringing all possible controversies between the parties before the Court for complete and effective adjudication of the matter and to avoid multiplicity of litigations. The object is that the Court should try the merits of the case that comes before it and consequently allow all amendments that may be necessary to determine the real question in controversy between the parties provided it does not cause injustice or prejudice to the other side. And when such amendment is allowed, it relates back or takes effect on and from the date of filling of the suit.</u>

<u>17. In the present case after filling of the suit the plaintiffs were dispossessed which the Courts concurrently found to have been proved along with the title of the plaintiffs. So it is immaterial whether the plaintiffs prayed for amendment of the plaint stating the date of dispossession during the pendency of the suit for declaration of title filed on 19.07.1977 band praying for recovery of Khas possession after laps of some year. The Courts below concurrently found that the plaintiff have been able to prove that they have title to and were in possession of the suit plot till they were dispossessed on 10.10.1977 during the pendency of the suit. This dispossession is a subsequent development during the pendency of the suit which has come before the Court and has become necessary to determine the real question in controversy between the parties. If the same is not allowed the parties to the suit would be prejudiced and would cause injustice to the plaintiffs which would lead to multiplicity of litigations. So it is not proper to conclude that suit was barred by limitation for amending the plaint of 25.02.1992. Because the moment it is allowed under the general principal of law it will relate back to the filling of the suit. In the case of Shishil Ranjan Dutta Vs. Alhaj Molvi Idris Mia reported in 42 DLR (AD) 110 this Division held once an amendment of the plaint is allowed the amendment will relate back to the date of the institution of the suit and will be operative from that date. So on this score it cannot be said that the suit was barred by limitation or was not maintainable since admittedly the plaintiffs were in possession of the same when the suit was instituted. Apart from this, when on scrutinizing the evidence on record both the Courts found the plaintiffs to be in possession and the allegation of being dispossessed on a particular date during the pendency of the suit is also found to be correct and proved it is immaterial as to when such amendment has been sought for or made.</u>

<u>18. The only thing is to be locked into in this case is whether at the time of filling of the suit the plaintiffs were in possession of the suit land and during the pendency of the suit land and during the pendency of the suit whether they have been dispossessed. When the same is found to be correct and proved then the amendment sought for at any stage of the suit or at any time before the issues are framed on the basis of pleading of parties and evidence are adduced that will be sufficient for the purpose of disposal of the suit upon adjudicating all the issues framed accordingly including the issue of possession and dispossession. In the present case while framing the issues on the basis of the pleading of both the parties for proper and final adjudication of the dispute the trial court specifically framed issue on whether the plaintiffs were in possession of the suit land and whether they have been dispossessed on the date as alleged by the plaintiffs and whether they were entitles to recovery of khas possession in the suit land the Courts below having found the plain-tiffs case of the issues having been found in favour of the plaintiffs the suit cannot be dismissed on the ground of limitation holding that the prayer for recovery of khas possession has been sought for after 12 years from the date of dispossession in a suit which is pending since before dispossession. Allowing or refusing amendment is an inherent power of the Court (Kangamal Vs, Panchapakesa, 23 Indian Cases, 82). The Court has been given vide discretion to determine the same of course within the terms of the Rule (Order Vi Rule 17) as decided in the case of Dr. Abdur Rahman Vs, Bangladesh (30 DLR (AD) 93). The Court has to exercise the discretion on the facts and circumstances of each case keeping in mind the principal of advancing substantial justice is of prime importance. Under such circumstances the trial court was thus wrong in dismissing the suit on the ground of limitation. The view taken by the appellate court was fully correct. But, the High Court Division felt in error in making the Rule absolute and thereby in setting aside the judgment and decree of the lower appellate court.</u>

19. For the reasons stated hereinabove we are the view that the finding and decision arrived at by the High Court Division being not based on proper appreciation of facts, evidence and law the same is liable to be set aside.

20. Accordingly, this civil appeal is allowed. The impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is set aside and those of the court of appeal below are restored. However there will be no order as to costs.

End.
